verdict: Jack Henry grew revenue 9% to $702M and net income 11% to $160M as banks and credit unions kept moving onto its cloud — card, digital and faster-payments volumes all climbed.

segments.name: Services & support
segments.note: Software, hosting and support for core banking systems — hosting revenue grew 11.7% as clients migrate to Jack Henry's private cloud.

segments.name: Processing
segments.note: Per-transaction processing: card revenue +9.4%, digital and transaction revenue +13.3%, and faster payments revenue +43.8%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the next generation of banking software and payments.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling to banks and credit unions, plus the back office.

otherDetail: Net interest income of $4M — $5M of interest income less $2M of interest expense.

takeaways.title: Faster payments is taking off
takeaways.text: Faster-payments revenue jumped 43.8% on expanding transaction volumes, while digital revenue rose 13.3% and card revenue 9.4%.

takeaways.title: The cloud shift continues
takeaways.text: Hosting revenue grew 11.7% as new and existing clients migrate from on-premise systems to Jack Henry's private cloud.

takeaways.title: Steady buybacks
takeaways.text: Jack Henry repurchased $71M of stock in the quarter at an average of $153.47 per share, with only $85M of debt outstanding.

oneTimers: Revenue includes $18M of deconversion fees — one-time payments from institutions that left the platform, nearly double last year's $9M. Excluding them (and a small acquisition), non-GAAP adjusted revenue grew 7.2%.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M from Jack Henry's thousands-denominated statement; the tax line absorbs a $1M rounding difference so the lines add exactly.
